analysis.evidence: Abram opens with בִּלְעָדַי, then uses רַק to allow for what the young men have eaten and for his companions’ share. הֵם יִקְחוּ חֶלְקָם (‘they shall take their share’) makes clear whose share he preserves.
analysis.morphology: The preposition takes a first-person common singular suffix referring to Abram.
analysis.sense: Abram excludes himself from receiving a share of the spoil.

analysis.evidence: After בִּלְעָדַי, Abram uses רַק to qualify his refusal. He makes an exception for what the young men ate and for the share due to the men who went with him.
analysis.morphology: Restrictive particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In רַק אֲשֶׁר אָכְלוּ הַנְּעָרִים, “only what the young men ate,” הַנְּעָרִים is the subject of אָכְלוּ. אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause with no expressed antecedent and identifies what they ate.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר אָכְלוּ הַנְּעָרִים means “what the young men ate.” Abram excepts what they have already consumed from the goods he declines to take.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural. The ending וּ agrees with the plural subject הַנְּעָרִים.

analysis.evidence: Abram sets aside what the young men ate during the expedition. He then claims a separate share for his named allies, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. The young men are Abram’s own fighting party.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine plural absolute noun. The dagesh in נ marks the doubling caused by the article.
analysis.sense: young men serving as fighting men

analysis.evidence: The closing clause הֵם יִקְחוּ חֶלְקָם, “they shall take their share,” confirms that חֵלֶק denotes the portion of goods the men may claim.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ means “and.” The masculine singular noun חֵלֶק is in construct with הָאֲנָשִׁים, giving “and the men’s share.”
analysis.sense: The share of the recovered goods due to the men who accompanied Abram.

analysis.evidence: The clause אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ אִתִּי, “who went with me,” identifies the men. Abram then names them individually as Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre and says they may take their share.
analysis.morphology: הָ is the definite article. אֲנָשִׁים is the irregular masculine plural absolute of אִישׁ.

analysis.evidence: In הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ אִתִּי, “the men who went with me,” אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause describing the men. They are the subject of the plural verb הָלְכוּ.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ אִתִּי means “who went with me.” Abram identifies Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre as the men who accompanied him and may take their share.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, agreeing with הָאֲנָשִׁים (“the men”).

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for עָנֵר. Leave its root unassigned because the derivation is uncertain.
draft.definition: Aner, brother of Mamre and covenant partner of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:13 identifies Aner through his kinship with Mamre and his covenant with Abram.

analysis.evidence: Abram names Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre as the men who went with him and are entitled to their share. The same three men appear as Abram’s allies in Genesis 14:13.
analysis.morphology: Masculine personal name in apposition to הָאֲנָשִׁים, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Aner, brother of Mamre and ally of Abram

draft.change: Add a personal-name article. The source gloss “young camel” has no support in the verse, and the source root אשה has no established connection to the name.
draft.definition: Eshcol, brother of Mamre and ally of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:13 identifies Eshcol by kinship with Mamre. Genesis 14:24 names Aner, Eshcol and Mamre together as the men who went with Abram.

analysis.evidence: Abram names Eshcol between Aner and Mamre among the men who went with him and are to receive their share. Genesis 14:13 identifies Eshcol as Mamre’s brother.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Eshcol, Mamre’s brother and Abram’s ally
